title: Environment values reach the verifier, preview and deploy spawns merged under the wrapper allowlist, and never reach the log
description:
SPIDR grandchild A of task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1 (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05), split because the parent measured over the file cap across four subsystems. This row is THE DELIVERY HALF and it is self-contained: it owns the parent's DoD 1, 2 and 5. It carries the parent's dependsOn unchanged (task-d0c63cd8 the store, DONE; task-a2409cba the published commands, BLOCKED at filing).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the plaintext delivery read that child 1 deliberately did NOT export, the merge of environment values into the spawn environment UNDER the existing allowlist, and the spawn half of the canary.

THE PLAINTEXT READ DOES NOT EXIST YET AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts's header states "NO PLAINTEXT-RETURNING FUNCTION IS EXPORTED FROM THIS MODULE. Delivering values into spawns is a separate concern and a separate row." THIS IS THAT ROW. The primitive exists - `openEnvironmentValue` at apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-cipher.ts:132 - and the read side already opens every seal to derive its fingerprint (environment-projection.ts:89-95) and then DROPS the plaintext. This row adds the one function that returns it, and it should be a NEW focused module so the no-plaintext property of environment-store.ts stays true and greppable.

MERGED UNDER THE ALLOWLIST, NOT AROUND IT. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.ts` builds a child env from a CLOSED roster: RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS (:14), PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES (:28), and it scrubs every `MOE_*` key (:56). `agentEnvironment()` returns that object. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.ts:67` reads `options.environment ?? process.env` and passes `env: environment` at :154. Environment values JOIN that construction; a delivery that hands a child `process.env` plus extras destroys the allowlist's whole purpose and would be very hard to notice.

NOTE THE `MOE_*` SCRUB (:56) when choosing the canary variable name: `agentEnvironment` drops every key starting with MOE_, so a canary named `MOE_CANARY_<random>` would be scrubbed by the very construction under test and the arm would pass for the wrong reason. Measure the scrub before naming the canary, and if the parent's suggested name is scrubbed, pick one that is not and say so.

NOT IN SCOPE: the required variable NAMES from the contract and the `.env.example` file (grandchild C, which waits on grandchild B); no UI (parent's child 3).

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: The verifier, preview and deploy spawns receive the environment's variables MERGED UNDER the existing allowlist construction (agent-spawn-environment.ts / verifier-process-runner.ts), not appended to a raw process.env. A test asserts the child's env CONTAINS the delivered variable AND STILL EXCLUDES a host variable outside the allowlist, on the same constructed env - the exclusion arm is what proves the merge did not widen the surface, and without it a passing test is compatible with handing the child everything.

THE SPAWN HALF OF THE CANARY, both directions in ONE test because they pull against each other: set a canary variable to a random value, spawn a verifier, and assert (a) the CHILD SAW the value, read from the CHILD'S OWN OUTPUT and never from the parent's intent, and (b) the value appears NOWHERE in the wrapper log bytes. A delivery that logs what it delivers is the obvious failure and only the pair catches it. The canary name must not be scrubbed by agent-spawn-environment.ts's MOE_ prefix scrub - state which name you used and why it survives.

A plaintext-returning delivery read exists in its OWN module, NOT added to environment-store.ts, whose header states that no plaintext-returning function is exported from it. Assert that property still holds after this row: a grep of environment-store.ts's exports shows no value-returning function.

AN ENVIRONMENT WITH NO VARIABLES SET DELIVERS NOTHING AND REFUSES NOTHING: a spawn with an empty environment must produce a child env byte-identical to what it produces today. Assert the byte-identity against the pre-existing construction, not merely that the spawn succeeded - the verifier ran fine before this feature and must not start depending on it.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: MERGE UNDER THE ALLOWLIST, NEVER AROUND IT. The closed roster exists so a child sees what it needs and nothing else. Never pass `process.env` plus extras, and never widen RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS or PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES to make a test pass.
THE VALUE REACHES THE CHILD AND NOT THE LOG. Assert both, from the child's own output and from the log bytes. One without the other is not evidence.
DELIVERY MUST NOT BECOME A DEPENDENCY: a project with no variables set must spawn exactly as it does today, asserted as byte-identity.

DO NOT ADD A PLAINTEXT-RETURNING FUNCTION TO environment-store.ts. Its header makes the no-plaintext claim and a canary suite greps it. Put the delivery read in a new focused module with a one-line .js bridge.
Mind the MOE_ scrub at agent-spawn-environment.ts:56 when naming the canary variable, or the arm passes for the wrong reason.
NO required-variable NAMES, NO .env.example, NO UI - those are grandchildren B and C and the parent's child 3.

implementationPlan.description: THE DELIVERY READ, IN ITS OWN MODULE. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-delivery.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (rail 4 asks for the bridge by name; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). THIS MODULE EXISTS SO A PROPERTY STAYS TRUE: `environment-store.ts`'s header states that NO PLAINTEXT-RETURNING FUNCTION IS EXPORTED FROM IT, and a canary suite greps that file. Adding the read there would falsify a claim another test depends on - which is why child 1 deliberately left this out. Export ONE function returning the environment's variables as plaintext `{name: value}`. Build it on `openEnvironmentValue` (environment-cipher.ts:132), whose docblock records the property to preserve: a wrong credential, a flipped byte, a replayed salt and a swapped tag ALL land on AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with NO BYTES RELEASED, because GCM verifies before it yields. Do not soften that - a delivery that returns partial plaintext on a tampered seal is worse than one that refuses. `environment-projection.ts:89-95` already opens every seal to derive a fingerprint and then DROPS the plaintext; read it and follow the same opening path rather than inventing a second one. DECIDE AND STATE what the read does when ONE seal of several fails to open: refusing the whole delivery is defensible, delivering the rest is defensible, silently skipping is not. Say which and why in the docblock - a spawn that quietly receives three of four variables is the kind of thing that is diagnosed at 2am. Write the module's header to state its one job and to name why it is not in environment-store.ts, so the next reader does not tidy it back in.
implementationPlan.note:
NEW MODULE `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-delivery.ts` (148 lines, well under the 250 target) plus its `.js` bridge. environment-store.ts NOT touched, so its "NO PLAINTEXT-RETURNING FUNCTION IS EXPORTED FROM THIS MODULE" header stays true and greppable; the new module's header says in as many words why it is not in the store and tells the next reader not to tidy it back in.

BRIDGE BYTES ARE EXACT. `export * from "./environment-delivery.ts";\n` - verified with `cat -A` to be byte-shaped like the sibling `environment-cipher.js`, and equal to `expectedBridgeSource()` at runtime-entrypoint.test.ts:207-212. Creating environment-delivery.test.ts in step 4 promotes this module to the runtime tier via the test-SIBLING rule (:159-160), which is exactly why the bridge ships now rather than later.

TWO EXPORTS, and they are deliberately separate concerns:
  1. `readEnvironmentDelivery(config, environment)` - THE plaintext read. Reuses `admitEnvironment` for scope -> key -> openability so a delivery read refuses with the same codes from the same layers as every other entry point, then re-opens each current seal via `openEnvironmentValue` and decodes. Follows environment-projection.ts:95-112's opening path rather than inventing a second one.
  2. `deliverEnvironment(allowlisted, delivered)` -> `{ collisions, environment }` - the merge, so the rule is written ONCE for all three spawn constructions instead of drifting three ways. (The two verbatim-copied private `runtimeEnvironment` functions in the runner and the preview process are the existing proof that a duplicated rule here drifts.)

DECISION 1 - PARTIAL OPEN: **ONE UNOPENABLE SEAL REFUSES THE WHOLE DELIVERY**, code ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE, zero variables returned, and the partial map built so far is discarded with it. Recorded in the header and at the branch. Reasons, both written down: (i) environment-projection.ts:89-94 already fixed this rule for the metadata read in the same words ("A single unopenable record fails the WHOLE read: reporting the openable subset would let a partially-unreadable store look healthy"), and a second, looser rule for the more dangerous surface would be indefensible; (ii) delivery has the stronger version of the problem - a spawn that quietly gets three of four variables fails hours later and far from here; (iii) returning "the ones that worked" would convert `openEnvironmentValue`'s fail-CLOSED guarantee into a fail-OPEN feature at the one call site that matters. Silent skipping was never on the table.

DECISION 2 - COLLISIONS (needed by step 3, settled here because the rule belongs with the merge): **THE ALLOWLISTED RUNTIME VALUE WINS AND THE COLLISION IS REPORTED BY NAME.** The store admits `PATH` - `ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_NAME_PATTERN` is `/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/u` and reserves nothing - so an operator can name a variable `PATH`, `COMSPEC` or `SYSTEMROOT`. Letting it through hands an operator-controlled value the choice of WHICH `node` and WHICH shell the daemon's own verifier spawns: privilege escalation dressed as configuration. Refusing the entire spawn is the other defensible answer and I rejected it in the header: a preview that will not start because someone named a variable `TEMP` is an outage, and the safe half is reachable without one. Silence was NOT an option, so `collisions` is a RETURNED field, not a comment - names are already non-secret (`EnvironmentVariableRead` has always carried `name`), so an operator surface can later say exactly which variable was not delivered. Membership is tested with `in`, not truthiness: an allowlisted key deliberately set to `""` is still the runtime's answer and must not be displaced by a quieter route.

DECISION 3 - BYTE-IDENTITY BY CONSTRUCTION: with nothing to deliver, `deliverEnvironment` returns THE VERY OBJECT it was handed, by reference. Not a copy, not a spread, not a re-ordered key set, no undefined-valued slot. DoD-4 therefore cannot be broken by an accidental unconditional overlay - there is no code path that touches the object when `delivered` is undefined or empty. Step 4 asserts it anyway, and step 5 drill (iii) mutates exactly this branch.

NO VALUE ON ANY FAILURE PATH: refusals come from `environmentRefusal` (fixed prose keyed by code, never interpolated); nothing here logs, and nothing throws a value. Plaintext exists in exactly two places, both named in the header: the returned `variables` map and the child environment built from it.

GATE: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0, with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` script echo as execution evidence.

implementationPlan.description: THE MERGE, AND THE THING THAT MAKES 'UNDER THE ALLOWLIST' AMBIGUOUS. Wire delivery into the spawn environment at the site(s) step 1(a) settled. READ THIS FIRST: an operator's variable names are ARBITRARY (`DATABASE_URL`, `STRIPE_KEY`), so they are NOT in `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` and do NOT match `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES`. Passing them through `agentEnvironment(source)` or `runtimeEnvironment(source)` DROPS EVERY ONE OF THEM - the closed roster is doing exactly its job. So 'merged UNDER the allowlist' cannot mean 'passed through the filter'; it means APPLIED TO THE OBJECT THE FILTER RETURNS, after the allowlist construction has done its work. A worker who reads it the other way gets a test where the delivered variable never arrives, and the tempting next move is to widen `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` - WHICH RAIL 1 FORBIDS IN THOSE WORDS. Never widen either roster to make a test pass. The shape is: build the allowlisted env exactly as today, then overlay the delivered variables onto that result. DECIDE THE COLLISION RULE AND STATE IT: what happens when a delivered variable has the same name as an allowlisted host variable (`PATH`, say, or `HOME`). An operator variable silently overriding PATH is a foot-gun; refusing it, or refusing to overwrite an allowlisted key, is defensible. Pick one, write it in the docblock, and give it a test arm - this is the kind of decision that is invisible until it breaks a spawn. KEEP THE HOST FILES SMALL: verifier-process-runner.ts is 395 lines against a 400 cap - FIVE lines of headroom - so the merge logic goes in the new module and the call site is one line. agent-spawn-environment.ts is 83 lines and has room, but the same rule applies: one construction, called from both sites, beats two copies that drift.
implementationPlan.note:
MERGE WIRED AT ALL THREE SITES, THROUGH ONE SHARED FUNCTION. Every call site is `deliverEnvironment(<the filter's RESULT>, delivered)` - the overlay lands on the object the allowlist construction RETURNED, never on the `process.env` it was given. NEITHER ROSTER WAS TOUCHED: `git diff` shows zero changes to RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS (any of the three copies) or PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES.

1. verifier-process-runner.ts - new `delivered?: EnvironmentDeliveredVariables` option (first member, keeping the interface's alphabetical order), and :70 is now `const { environment } = deliverEnvironment(runtimeEnvironment(sourceEnvironment), options.delivered);`. Everything downstream (`env: environment` at the spawn) is untouched.
2. preview/preview-process.ts - same option on `PreviewProcessOptions`, and the `env:` argument at the `spawn(...)` call is now `deliverEnvironment(runtimeEnvironment(sourceEnvironment), options.delivered).environment`.
3. agent-spawn-environment.ts - `agentEnvironment(source, delivered?)` gains an OPTIONAL second parameter and returns `deliverEnvironment(environment, delivered).environment`. Applied LAST, after the four added keys, so it is the finished object that gets overlaid.

WHY agentEnvironment's DELIVERY IS OPT-IN AND agent-spawner.ts PASSES NOTHING. `agentEnvironment` feeds CODING-AGENT seats, not a deploy target. Wiring an operator's production secrets into every coding seat by default would widen a secret's blast radius far past what DoD-1 asks for, and rail 3 of this epic is about where a secret may surface. So the parameter exists (the construction is capable, one line from any future caller) and both existing call sites - agent-spawner.ts:156 and :159 - are LEFT UNCHANGED and therefore byte-identical. The two real production consumer edges for the new module are the verifier and preview spawns.

LINE CAPS, before -> after: verifier-process-runner.ts **395 -> 399** (cap 400; ONE line of headroom left, and it cost three rounds of trimming - a two-line import became one, a five-line destructure became one, and the option's JSDoc became a trailing comment). preview-process.ts 296 -> 300. agent-spawn-environment.ts 81 -> 91. environment-delivery.ts 148. All under 400; only the runner is anywhere near it, which is exactly why the merge logic is in the new module and each call site is a single expression.

A BUG I INTRODUCED AND FIXED INSIDE THIS STEP, recorded because it is the kind that survives review: to keep the options interface alphabetical I inserted `delivered` above `drainGraceMs` - which silently re-parented `drainGraceMs`'s five-line JSDoc onto `delivered`, so the drain-grace explanation would have documented the wrong field. Caught by reading the region back rather than by any gate; typecheck cannot see it. `delivered` now sits above the JSDoc block, which stays attached to `drainGraceMs`.

COLLISION RULE (decided and documented in step 2, this is where it takes effect): the allowlisted runtime value WINS and the delivered name is reported in `collisions`. So a delivered `PATH` cannot change which `node` or which shell the daemon's own verifier spawns. Test arm in step 4; the returned `collisions` field is what keeps it from being silent.

GATE: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` script echo. Full suite runs in step 5 - deliberately not run mid-edit, since this package's suite takes ~10 minutes and an edit landing during its 6-minute import phase would poison the result.

implementationPlan.description: THE TESTS, AND THE CANARY IS ONE TEST FOR A REASON. (1) DoD-2, THE CANARY, BOTH DIRECTIONS IN ONE TEST because they pull against each other: set a variable to a random value, spawn a verifier, and assert (a) THE CHILD SAW IT, read from THE CHILD'S OWN OUTPUT - never from the parent's intent, never from the env object you constructed, because asserting the object you just built proves only that you built it; and (b) the value appears NOWHERE in the wrapper log bytes. Split into two tests, each half can pass while the other fails and nobody notices; together they are the property. Use the name step 1(c) proved survives the MOE_ scrub at BOTH sites, and say in a comment why that name and not `MOE_CANARY_*`. (2) DoD-1's PAIR, and the exclusion half is the load-bearing one: on the SAME constructed env, assert the delivered variable IS present AND a host variable outside the allowlist is STILL ABSENT. Without the exclusion arm, a passing test is compatible with having handed the child `process.env` plus extras - which is the failure rail 1 exists to prevent and is very hard to notice in review. (3) DoD-4, BYTE-IDENTITY: with an environment that has NO variables set, the constructed child env is byte-identical to what the pre-existing construction produces. Assert equality against the OLD construction's output, not merely that the spawn succeeded - the verifier ran fine before this feature and must not start depending on it. This is the arm that catches an unconditional overlay that adds an empty object, a key with an undefined value, or a reordered object. (4) DoD-3: a grep of `environment-store.ts`'s exports shows no value-returning function - assert it as source text the way `goal-publish.test.tsx` pins its no-localStorage property, so the claim in that file's header stays true and greppable. (5) The collision rule from step 3 and the partial-open decision from step 2, each with an arm asserting the behaviour you chose.

TESTS LANDED. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run ... src/environment src/orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.test.ts src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.test.ts` -> exit 0, count line **`Test Files  10 passed (10)`** / `Tests  188 passed (188)`.

A first run reported 41 tests in 201ms, which cannot include a real child process, so I re-ran with `--reporter=verbose`: **`the delivery canary > reaches the spawned child and appears in no log or capture byte  502ms`** and `Tests  18 passed (18)` for the delivery file. The canary spawns a real `node probe.mjs`; the 502ms is the child. Before writing it I prototyped the spawn shape standalone on this host (`shell: true` + cmd.exe + a filtered env) and confirmed `sha256("abc123")` came back from the child, so the test was not written against a guess about Windows quoting.

(1) DoD-2 THE CANARY - ONE test, both arms, `environment-delivery.test.ts`. Sets `DEPLOY_CANARY_TOKEN` to `canary-<24 random bytes>`, spawns a real verifier whose probe prints `CANARY_DIGEST=sha256(value)`.
  - Arm (a), from THE CHILD'S OWN OUTPUT: `expect(capturedOutput).toContain("CANARY_DIGEST=" + sha256(secret))`. Never the env object I constructed - asserting that would only prove I built it.
  - NEGATIVE CONTROL beside it: `not.toContain("CANARY_DIGEST=ABSENT")`, so a delivery that never happened reads as a failure rather than as a quiet pass.
  - Arm (b), NOWHERE IN THE LOG: `process.stdout.write` and `process.stderr.write` are spied for the duration and every chunk collected. That IS the wrapper log's bytes rather than a stand-in - `agent-wrapper-main.ts` wires all four of its `log` sinks to exactly those two calls (:136, :162, :235, :289). Asserted STRONGER than DoD-2 asks: the secret is also absent from the run capture and from the workspace file the child ran.
  - WHY THE CHILD PRINTS A DIGEST RATHER THAN THE VALUE, written into the test header: only a process holding the exact bytes can produce `sha256(value)`, so it still proves receipt from the child's own output - and it keeps the raw secret out of EVERY byte, which is what lets arm (b) assert the strict superset instead of having to carve out the child's own echo. Printing the secret to prove it arrived would also put it on a screen and into a CI transcript, which this epic's third rail forbids in those words.
  - NAME: `DEPLOY_CANARY_TOKEN`, with the reasoning in a comment at the constant - not `MOE_CANARY_*` because agent-spawn-environment.ts:54 scrubs `MOE_`, which would fail arm (a) and pass arm (b) for the wrong reason. It is also in NO roster and matches NO provider prefix, so it can only arrive by the overlay.

THREE MEASURED FINDINGS, ONE ACTIONABLE NOW BY A GOVERNOR. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 5 files (2 new).

## 1. "Merged UNDER the allowlist" is ambiguous, and the obvious reading is broken

An operator's variable names are arbitrary — `DATABASE_URL`, `STRIPE_KEY`. They are **not** in `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` and do **not** match `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES`. So passing them through `agentEnvironment(source)` or `runtimeEnvironment(source)` **drops every one of them** — the closed roster doing exactly its job.

The merge must be applied to the object the filter **returns**, not to its input. A worker who reads it the other way gets a test where nothing arrives, and the tempting next move is widening the roster — which rail 1 forbids in those words. Named in step 3.

## 2. There are TWO allowlist constructions, and DoD-1 names both files as if they shared one

```
agent-spawn-environment.ts:53   agentEnvironment()     key set OR provider prefix,
                                                       scrubs MOE_*, ADDS 4 keys
verifier-process-runner.ts:377  runtimeEnvironment()   PRIVATE. key set ALONE.
                                                       no prefixes, no scrub, no additions
```

And `:68` shows the verifier spawn uses the **private** one. Wiring delivery into `agentEnvironment` and assuming the verifier is covered leaves that spawn undelivered while the test passes. Step 1 makes the worker confirm both and decide deliberately whether to unify them.

**Consequence for the canary:** the `MOE_*` scrub exists at one site and not the other, so a name can behave differently at each. The plan requires a name that survives **both**. (Scrub confirmed at `agent-spawn-environment.ts:56`; the row's warning is correct.)

## 3. The `dependsOn` on task-a2409cba (BLOCKED) looks unnecessary — governor call

`environment-store.ts` **exports** `setEnvironmentVariable`:117 and `unsetEnvironmentVariable`:146, so this row's tests can seed values with no command kind at all. None of the five DoD items dispatches a command — this is the delivery **read** path, not the operator write path. The dependency that matters, `task-d0c63cd8` (the store), is **DONE**.

If that holds, dropping `task-a2409cba` makes this row claimable now instead of gated behind a blocked chain. I did not edit `dependsOn` myself: the row is claimed for PLANNING and a dependency change while another architect's chain is mid-flight is a governor's call. Step 1 has the worker confirm and raise it.

## Two behaviours the row leaves undecided, and neither should be an accident

- **A delivered variable named `PATH`.** Silently overriding an allowlisted host value is a foot-gun; refusing it is defensible. Pick one, document it, test it.
- **One seal of several failing to open.** Refuse the whole delivery, or deliver the rest — both defensible. **Silently skipping is not**: a spawn quietly receiving three of four variables is diagnosed at 2am.

## Constraints and drills

`verifier-process-runner.ts` is **395 lines against a 400 cap** — five lines of headroom, so the merge logic goes in the new module and the call site is one line.

The row's load-bearing drill is (i): make the merge hand the child `process.env` plus extras. The **delivery** arm still passes; the **exclusion** arm must go red. That pair is the only thing between this feature and a silently widened process surface — and if the exclusion arm stays green it is not testing what it claims.

So `MOE_CANARY_*` is dropped by `agentEnvironment` and NOT by `runtimeEnvironment` - the canary name must survive both.

THE PRIMITIVE AND ITS PROPERTY: `openEnvironmentValue(credential, sealed)` at environment-cipher.ts:132, whose docblock states the fail-closed guarantee - a wrong credential, a flipped ciphertext byte, a replayed salt and a swapped tag ALL land on AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with NO BYTES RELEASED, because GCM verifies before it yields. `environment-projection.ts:89-95` already opens every seal for a fingerprint and drops the plaintext - the existing opening path to follow.

5. THE LINE-CAP CONSTRAINT: verifier-process-runner.ts is 395 lines against a 400 cap - FIVE lines of headroom. The merge logic cannot live there. agent-spawn-environment.ts is 83, environment-store.ts 172.

6. THE VERIFIER SPAWNS WITH `shell: true` (verifier-process-runner.ts:151) - relevant to the adversarial pass on a delivered value containing a shell metacharacter, though whether that is this row's problem or the runner owner's is a judgement the worker should record rather than silently absorb.

planningNotes.risks:
FIRST - THE MERGE READ THE WRONG WAY DROPS EVERY VARIABLE, and the tempting fix is the one rail 1 forbids. Operator names are arbitrary and therefore not on either closed roster; passing them through the filter deletes them. Overlay onto the filter's OUTPUT. Never widen `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` or `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES` to make an arm pass.

SECOND - WIRING ONE CONSTRUCTION AND ASSUMING THE OTHER. `agentEnvironment` and `runtimeEnvironment` are different functions with different rules, and the verifier uses the private one. Delivery wired only into the first leaves the verifier spawn undelivered while a test against the first passes.

THIRD - THE EXCLUSION ARM IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF DoD-1. Asserting only that the delivered variable arrived is compatible with having handed the child `process.env` plus extras. Drill (i) reproduces exactly that and requires the exclusion arm to red.

FOURTH - ASSERTING THE OBJECT YOU BUILT PROVES NOTHING. DoD-2 says read from the CHILD'S OWN OUTPUT; a test that inspects the constructed env object proves only that it was constructed. And splitting the canary into two tests lets either half rot unnoticed - it is one test because the two halves pull against each other.

FIFTH - THE MOE_ SCRUB WOULD MAKE THE CANARY PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON at one of the two sites. Measure, then name.

SIXTH - DELIVERY MUST NOT BECOME A DEPENDENCY. An unconditional overlay that adds an empty object, an undefined-valued key, or a reordered object breaks byte-identity for a project with no variables. Assert identity against the OLD construction's output, not spawn success.

SEVENTH - TWO BEHAVIOURS ARE UNDECIDED AND MUST NOT BE ACCIDENTS: what a delivered variable named `PATH` does to an allowlisted host value, and what happens when one seal of several fails to open. Silent skipping is the wrong answer to the second in every case - a spawn quietly receiving three of four variables is diagnosed at 2am.

EIGHTH - FIVE LINES OF HEADROOM in verifier-process-runner.ts (395/400). The merge logic belongs in the new module; the call site is one line.

NINTH - THE LOG IS NOT THE ONLY LEAK SURFACE. A value can reach a receipt, an error message, a stack trace or a crash path's output. The canary covers the log; the adversarial pass must look at the others.

TENTH - shared checkout. Peer dirt under .moe/ and .grok/ is NEVER a stop condition: note it, never revert, stash or `git add -A`. Report every path you touch in complete_step.modifiedFiles, including the new module and its bridge.
